official.deadline_central_display: Varies by programme; the Commission states that in most cases applications run from October to January for courses starting the following academic year
official.deadline_note: There is no single Commission-wide deadline: each consortium running the joint master publishes its own admission and scholarship deadlines, and the Commission advises applying between October and January for the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Annual; a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the catalogue each year
official.status_note: The Commission's student page is live and directs applicants to the current EMJM catalogue and to each consortium's own application portal.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Commission's student page states that 'Masters may also offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide' and that 'Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance'; it does not itemise tuition, which is set by each consortium.
benefits: Full scholarship to the best-ranked students worldwide
EU scholarship for individuals: EUR 1,400 per month, maximum 24 months
eligibility: Students from all over the world are welcome
Must hold a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in the last year of bachelor studies
Must graduate before the master's programme starts
A bachelor's equivalent level of learning may be accepted if officially recognised in the degree-awarding country
Applicants apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme
requirements: Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme via that master's website
Hold a bachelor's degree, or complete it before the programme starts
Follow the application steps published by each consortium, for the scholarship route and the non-scholarship route
documents: Each master's website publishes its own list of required application documents and steps; the Commission does not publish a common document list
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded to the best-ranked students worldwide
Ranking and selection are run by the consortium delivering the joint master
coverage: A living allowance of EUR 1,400 per month, for a maximum of 24 months
application_method: Search the EMJM course catalogue for programmes with Czech partners
Open the master's own website for entry requirements, deadlines and application steps
Submit the application directly to the institution running the programme
official.application_route: Search the Commission's EMJM catalogue, then apply directly to the consortium running the programme - there is no central Commission application.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction; students from all countries worldwide may apply
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the Commission states students from all over the world are welcome
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits); scholarship paid for a maximum of 24 months
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international masters, jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions, involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, and typically including periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence.
official.program_type: EU-funded joint master's degree delivered by an international consortium, with competitive EU scholarships

applicant_utility.summary: Approach this as a set of separate consortium applications where a Czech university is one partner, not as one Czech award. Because the ranking is run by each consortium, your motivation letter has to name that consortium's mobility route and research topics rather than generic praise for studying in the Czech Republic. The one Commission-wide number you can rely on is EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months, which is a unit cost and not a budget matched to Prague rents.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students or recent graduates who want a master's built around studying in more than one country, can meet a Czech partner's language and transcript requirements, and are willing to run several separate consortium applications in one October-January cycle.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist joint masters in the EACEA catalogue that include a Czech university, then open each consortium's own admissions page
Build a per-consortium deadline tracker for October to January, since the Commission sets no common date
Check the consortium's published language requirement for the Czech semester specifically, not just the language of instruction
Confirm your bachelor's will be complete before the programme starts and that it is recognisable in the degree-awarding country
Prepare a mobility justification explaining why you want that consortium's route through that specific Czech institution
common_rejection_risks: Assuming one Commission deadline and missing a consortium's earlier cut-off
Writing a motivation letter that applies equally to any European master, which reads badly in a consortium-ranked competition
Being in your last bachelor's year without evidence of a graduation date before the start
Assuming the EUR 1,400 monthly figure is sufficient for the Czech semester, particularly in Prague
Applying only through the scholarship route with no fallback if the consortium ranks you outside the awards
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and travel are only partly covered and tuition is set by each consortium, so installation costs, the gap between EUR 1,400 a month and actual rents, and any consortium charges remain yours.
document_audit: There is no Commission-wide document list; each consortium publishes its own, so build a separate pack per programme
Non-EU diplomas usually need translation and sometimes legalisation, and recognition in the degree-awarding country is a stated condition
If you are applying for the Czech semester, verify whether the consortium expects a Czech-semester-specific language certificate in addition to the teaching language certificate
alerts: An EMJM must involve at least three institutions from at least three different countries, so confirm the Czech partner's slot in the route before accepting
The Commission adds a new batch of selected masters to the catalogue each year, so a programme present now can disappear
The Commission describes these as prestigious programmes, and consortia expect a clear research fit in the motivation letter
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Identify the programme in the EACEA catalogue, apply to the running institution inside its own window, and let the consortium rank you for the scholarship - no Commission-level application exists.
